set.approach: Ahren's Rock is one of the Sunrise Crags, reached by the built trails and stairs that climb from the Crest Lake day-use area. The bolts are plain to see on the rock, and the route starts right above a wooden sign that reads Ahren's Rock.

review.notes: Sunrise Crags and Lower Sunrise pages: Crest Lake day-use area, bridge, signs up to Sunrise, built stairs; route page: starts above the wooden Ahren's Rock sign. Route can also be reached from the top (not a stated descent).

set.approach: Drive the Brandywine Creek forest road to the lower parking lot just before the bridge over Brandywine Creek, or on up the rougher road to the upper lot, which shortens the hike. Hike the summer trail up into Brandywine Meadows. At the flats, wade or step over the creek at the point the summer trail first touches it, then climb the west side of the meadows to a slab below Gato Negro. Arrogant Frog is the right-hand one of the two climbs on this formation.
set.descent_text: Either rappel the route or scramble off toward the south.

review.notes: Area page: roads and lots; route pages: creek crossing at the meadows, slab below Gato Negro, walk-off south or rappel. Rope length and distances left out.

set.approach: Drive the Brandywine Creek forest road to the lower parking lot just before the bridge over Brandywine Creek, or on up the rougher road to the upper lot, which shortens the hike. Hike the summer trail up into Brandywine Meadows. Bastardo is a long alpine sport route. The first pitch starts to the left of the fault and trends right, after a few moderate moves, to an anchor whose chains can be seen from below.

review.notes: Route page: first pitch description, rap options, bolted fourth-class descent section, advice to trend toward the ridge. Area page: lots. Approach time left out. Reconfirm at review that this reads as a descent. Lead review dropped the descent: too thin to stand.

set.approach: Drive the Brandywine Creek forest road to the lower parking lot just before the bridge over Brandywine Creek, or on up the rougher road to the upper lot, which shortens the hike. Hike the summer trail up into Brandywine Meadows. Copper Moon is a short way north of the three-pitch route Sheep. It starts just down and to the left of the old mine shaft.

review.notes: Area page: lots; route page: north of Sheep, left of the mine shaft. No descent stated.

set.approach: Drive the Brandywine Creek forest road to the lower parking lot just before the bridge over Brandywine Creek, or on up the rougher road to the upper lot, which shortens the hike. Hike the summer trail up into Brandywine Meadows. Cross the stream in the flats where the trail first reaches the creek, then climb up and to the right on faint trails to the base of the route, on a slab above the meadows.

review.notes: Area page: lots; route page: stream crossing, faint trails up and right, rappel the route (rope length left out).

set.approach: Drive the Brandywine Creek forest road to the lower parking lot just before the bridge over Brandywine Creek, or on up the rougher road to the upper lot, which shortens the hike. Hike the summer trail up into Brandywine Meadows. Get across the creek at the first spot the summer trail touches it, then climb the meadows' west side to the slab under Gato Negro. The route shares an anchor with Arrogant Frog, and its start is the one that snow can reach in early summer.
set.descent_text: Rappel Arrogant Frog from the shared anchor, walk off, or climb on up Gato Negro.

review.notes: Area page: lots; route pages: shared anchor with Arrogant Frog; descent options stated on this route page.

set.approach: Pull in at the Crest Lake day-use area, take the gravel road on the right, and park by the picnic area in the northwest corner of the lake. Cross the highway on foot and follow the trail east for a short distance to reach Crow's Nest. The route climbs the blocky arete with a series of small overhangs.
set.descent_text: Rappel from the anchors around the corner to the right, or walk off by climbing a cracked boulder and following the trail down to the right.

review.notes: Area page: parking and trail; route page: arete with small overhangs, rap or walk-off.

set.approach: Joint Wall is reached from the third pullout along the highway to Gold River; a trail descends from there to a rocky riverbed. The route begins up on a low fifth-class ledge, off to the left of the main wall. A side path on the wall's right climbs to the top, where top ropes can be rigged.

review.notes: Area page: access and side trail to top; route page: start on the ledge left of the main wall. No descent stated.

set.approach: Leave the car at the day-use area beside Crest Lake, walk over the bridge, and follow the signed trail. Lower Hidden Walls is the first set of climbs you come to. Midnight Rider is a bolted line to the left of Windweaver.

review.notes: Area page: parking, bridge, signs; route page: left of Windweaver. No descent stated.

set.approach: Leave the car at the day-use area beside Crest Lake, walk over the bridge, and follow the signed trail. Lower Hidden Walls is the first set of climbs you come to. This is the third route from the left on the ledge.

review.notes: Area page: parking, bridge, signs; route page: third from the left on the ledge. No descent stated.

set.approach: Leave the car at the day-use area beside Crest Lake, walk over the bridge, and follow the signed trail. Lower Hidden Walls is the first set of climbs you come to. Snakebite is on the slab below the obvious tree with a large root sticking out onto it.

review.notes: Area page: parking, bridge, signs; route page: below the tree with the big root. No descent stated.

set.approach: Leave the car at the day-use area beside Crest Lake, walk over the bridge, and follow the signed trail. Lower Hidden Walls is the first set of climbs you come to. This is the second route off the ledge.

review.notes: Area page: parking, bridge, signs; route page: second route off the ledge. No descent stated.

set.approach: Leave the car at the day-use area beside Crest Lake, walk over the bridge, and follow the signed trail. Follow the signs up toward Sunrise and bear right at the fork near the top to reach Lower Sunrise, a north-facing wall. It takes the bolted face midway across the formation.

review.notes: Area page: approach; route page: bolted face in the center. No descent stated.

set.approach: Approach through New Crest and follow the signs to the Hidden Walls; Middle Hidden Walls is the second tier of cliffs. The route is the last one on the Middle Hidden Wall before the trail climbs to the Upper Hiddens.

review.notes: Area page: approach; route page: last route before the trail rises to Upper Hiddens. No descent stated.

set.approach: Follow the climbers trail up through the forest. Where it leaves the trees, the Beehive Wall on the West Ridge is on your right, and the route is approached by a vegetated ledge a short hike up the hill. The first pitch joins the Beeline route for its first few bolts.
set.descent_text: Descend by rappelling the route on its bolted anchors. With a long rope two of the upper rappels can be combined, and the last rappel ends with a short easy downclimb to the ledge.

review.notes: Route page: approach from the climbers trail, Beehive Wall, rappel combinations. Counts and rope length left out.

set.approach: The approach is the same as for Time Machine: follow the climbers trail to where it leaves the forest, then keep circling the Beehive on its left side, then climb the snow or scree toward the little lake; the clean arete will be on your right.
set.descent_text: Rappel Time Machine. Ropes can jam on one of the rappels when two ropes are used.

review.notes: Route page states approach and descent (rap Time Machine). Upper pitches still being developed; only the stated approach and descent are used.

set.approach: Leave the car at the day-use area beside Crest Lake, walk over the bridge, and follow the signed trail. Follow the signs to Sunrise, and Salamander appears on your left. This is the second route on the wall.

review.notes: Area page: approach; route page: second route on the wall. No descent stated.

set.approach: Leave the car at the day-use area beside Crest Lake, walk over the bridge, and follow the signed trail. Follow the signs to Sunrise, and Salamander appears on your left. Middle Earth starts right of the crack and joins Hobbit Step partway up.

review.notes: Area page: approach; route page: start right of the crack, joins Hobbit Step. No descent stated.

set.approach: Leave the car at the day-use area beside Crest Lake, walk over the bridge, and follow the signed trail. Follow the signs to Sunrise, and Salamander appears on your left. It follows bolts on the face next to the prominent crack of Bitches Brew.

review.notes: Area page: approach; route page (the Crest Creek Salamander, not the West Virginia boulder problem of the same name): beside the crack of Bitches Brew. No descent stated.

set.approach: The hike starts from the lot at the Saint crag beside the road. Bear to climber's right of Saint and follow the flagged trail through the forest; the forest downhill of that point is private property, so stay on the trail. Work up the scree, keeping a narrow band of trees on your right, and follow the flagging and cairns to a fork with a cairn. Take the right-hand trail up through a second strip of trees, past a large log in the scree and a short thick patch of vegetation, then up loose scree to the base of Crystalline. The route begins where the flagging tape ends, above the treeline.
set.descent_text: You can rappel the route, or walk down from the top-out anchors on the descent trail, which is steep, heavily flagged and runs through the forest back to the parking lot.

review.notes: Area page: approach and descent trail, rappel option; route page: start where the flagging ends. Times, rap count and rope length left out.

set.approach: The hike starts from the lot at the Saint crag beside the road. Work up the scree, keeping a narrow band of trees on your right, and follow the flagging and cairns to a fork with a cairn. Take the right-hand trail up through a second strip of trees, past a large log in the scree and a short thick patch of vegetation, then up loose scree to the base of Crystalline. The route begins where the flagging tape ends, above the treeline. Show Goat is on Goat Ledge. Partway up Crystalline, carefully scramble up the steep dirt gully on the left to the foot of the ledge; one bolt at the gully's base protects the move if you prefer to stay roped. The route begins to the climber's right of a gully, on a belayer's platform that has been built up, so take care not to erode it.
set.descent_text: Rappel the route back down to Goat Ledge.

review.notes: Area page: approach to Goat Ledge and rappel to the ledge via this route; route page: start right of a gully.

set.approach: The hike starts from the lot at the Saint crag beside the road. Bear to climber's right of Saint and follow the flagged trail through the forest; the forest downhill of that point is private property, so stay on the trail. Work up the scree, keeping a narrow band of trees on your right, and follow the flagging and cairns to a fork with a cairn. Take the right-hand trail up through a second strip of trees, past a large log in the scree and a short thick patch of vegetation, then up loose scree to the base of Crystalline. The route begins where the flagging tape ends, above the treeline. Smoke Over Water is on the White Headwall. From the foot of Crystalline, keep angling up and right through the tangle of broken ground. The ground there is rather loose, with brief low-fifth-class steps possible. The first pitch is shared with Entourage Effect, and the second starts from their shared anchor.

review.notes: Area page: scramble to White Headwall; route page: shares pitch one with Entourage Effect. Descent for this route not stated.

set.approach: The hike starts from the lot at the Saint crag beside the road. Bear to climber's right of Saint and follow the flagged trail through the forest; the forest downhill of that point is private property, so stay on the trail. Work up the scree, keeping a narrow band of trees on your right, and follow the flagging and cairns to a fork with a cairn. Take the right-hand trail up through a second strip of trees, past a large log in the scree and a short thick patch of vegetation, then up loose scree to the base of Crystalline. The route begins where the flagging tape ends, above the treeline. Spirit of a Black Bear is on the upper wall above Crystalline, reached by scrambling up the steep dirt gully on the left partway up Crystalline (a bolt at the foot protects a fall). It finishes by joining the final stretch of Crystalline.
set.descent_text: Rappel the route back down to Goat Ledge, or finish up Crystalline and take the descent trail from the top-out anchors.

review.notes: Area page: approach, Goat Ledge access, rappel to ledge via this route, descent trail; route page: finishes into Crystalline.

From the big tree on the ledge, traverse along the thin ledge to climber's right to the start of the route.

review.notes: Area page: Goat Ledge access; route page: traverse a thin ledge right of the big tree. Descent for this route not stated.

set.approach: Access is from the third pullout on the highway toward Gold River. Take the trail down to the rocky riverbed. Sluice Wall lies close to Joint Wall on its right, where a path climbs a few steps. Yellow Ribbon is the second line up the wall and takes the main part of the overhang.
set.descent_text: The route has rappel anchors; rappel from them.

review.notes: Area page: approach; route page: second line, bolts plus rap anchors.

set.approach: The trail is steep with exposed sections and needs some scrambling. Drive Marion Creek Forest Service Road, turn right past the 5040 trailheads, and go to the far end of the parking area, where the trail starts. A fallen tree makes the river crossing simple, and several paths lead to it. From the high ground, climb the snow slope to the base of the northwest towers and aim for the steep section of darker rock, where the first belay station is.
set.descent_text: Rappel the route; every station has rap rings. Doubled ropes make the rappels full length and mostly free hanging, and the route can also be descended by the regular way down the towers.

review.notes: Area page: trail and river crossing; route page: snow slope to the northwest towers, rap rings, descent options. Rappel count and rope sizes left out (single source).
